A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same partial-adaptation study. Their complete main texts, four figures, four tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 18 language models on the authors' 21-dataset ICL benchmark and AlpacaEval 2.0, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised OLMo 2 AlpacaEval results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same interpolation between base and instruct weights. The partial-adaptation procedure and handling of Mixtral's additional tokens are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 21 general-domain and financial datasets across six task categories, plus AlpacaEval 2.0. Table 2 and Appendix A.1 retain the same coverage.

E2.justification: The same base and instruct comparators remain for all 18 models. GPT-4 Preview (11/06) remains the AlpacaEval reference; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The lambda grid, model configurations, dataset sizes, shot counts, templates, metrics, aggregation procedure, and May 2024 GPT-4o judge are unchanged. V2's main-text explanation of the 0–100 score scale repeats information already in v1 Appendix A.4.

E4.justification: The same interpolation sweeps and dataset-level comparisons remain. No new ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study is introduced; the OLMo 2 updates revise results within existing comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and curves without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 substantially revise the full OLMo 2 AlpacaEval trajectories. In Figure 3, instruct win rates change from approximately 12.6% to 35.0% for 7B and 8.9% to 42.9% for 13B. Table 1 changes their reported win-rate differences from -9.95 to -7.41 and -4.43 to -3.98 percentage points, respectively. ICL results, including Table 4, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The interpolation mathematics and Appendix A.2 equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. Metric-description edits correct wording without changing mathematical definitions; neither version adds proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: partial adaptation improves ICL performance, usually sacrifices instruction following, and can offer favorable tradeoffs at intermediate strengths.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly adds that AlpacaEval may not fully represent true instruction-following ability despite its correlation with Chatbot Arena. V1's limitations addressed ICL benchmark representativeness and English-only coverage without this additional qualification.

D1.justification: The Llama 3.2 reference changes its access destination from a release blog to model-card and prompt-format documentation. This is a limited access-information update; implementation instructions, calibration details, and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited studies and model references retain the same research positioning, including attribution of partial adaptation to Fleshman and Van Durme. Bibliographic dates, links, and citation formatting change without introducing new research contributions or comparisons.

P1.justification: V2 makes scattered grammatical and terminology corrections, refines several paragraphs, repeats the score-aggregation explanation in the main text, and updates an author's affiliation and email. The section sequence and overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 places Figures 3 and 4 together on page 14, whereas v1 separates them across pages 13–14. Appendix A.4's metrics are consolidated on page 13, with additional small caption and spacing edits. The figure and table inventory is unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves wording and explicitly qualifies AlpacaEval's representativeness, but its substantial OLMo 2 result revisions are unexplained. For OLMo 2 13B at lambda 6/8, v2 Table 1 reports a -3.98-point difference, while Figure 3 implies approximately -2.0 points. This unresolved numerical disagreement prevents a reliable net-quality judgment.
